div.head: Iud Dei XIV 11.1
div.ab: ut si de hoc furto noxius es, aut fecisti aut scisti aut consensisti aut inde peccatum habes, coniuro te per nomen sanctum Domini, ut panem uel caseum istum numquam possis manducare, sed inflatis buccis cum spuma et gemitu et lacrimis et dolore fauces tuae siccae efficiantur et obligent te, antequam confitearis peccata tua domino nostro Iesu Christo, qui uenturus est (iudicare uiuos et mortuos).
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 427 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

div.ab: that if you are guilty of this theft, or did it, or knew of it, or consented to it, or have sin from it, I conjure you by the holy name of the Lord that you may never be able to eat this bread or cheese, but, with swollen cheeks, with foam and groaning and tears and pain, may your jaws become dry and bind you, before you confess your sins to our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come (to judge the living and the dead).
